entities.summary:
Orontes IV. (b. 200 BCE, Sophene) was a prominent economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in Sophene. Known for his research on monarchs and rulers, Orontes IV. contributed significantly to the understanding of power dynamics in ancient civilizations.

Orontes IV.'s work was heavily influenced by the intellectual currents of his time, including the Sophistic movement and the rise of Hellenistic kingdoms. His findings had a lasting impact on the study of governance and statecraft, shaping the intellectual landscape of the ancient world.

The legacy of Orontes IV. can be seen in the continued study of monarchs and rulers throughout history, with his work remaining a vital source of insight for scholars and policymakers alike.

"The king is the god, and the people are his subjects," Orontes IV. once wrote, capturing the essence of the complex power dynamics that defined ancient civilizations.
